security_audit.summary: Static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, and app identifiers, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. Static network findings are documentation links and placeholder media URLs. The skill still carries medium contextual risk because it authorizes user-directed belt CLI calls and recommends installing a related CLI skill.

remediation.issue: External CLI processing of user content
remediation.suggestion: Document that belt sends prompts and media references to inference.sh or downstream model providers. Ask users to confirm before sending sensitive assets.
Replace npx install instructions with vetted marketplace dependencies or add clear source verification and user confirmation steps.

remediation.issue: Placeholder and external URLs in examples
remediation.suggestion: Label sample URLs as placeholders and remind users to use owned, public, or approved media assets.

content.user_title: Create AI Videos with Inference.sh Models
content.value_statement: Creating video workflows across many AI models can be slow and confusing. This skill organizes inference.sh model choices and belt CLI steps for video generation, animation, editing, and utilities.
actual_capabilities: Lists inference.sh video models for text-to-video, image-to-video, avatar, lipsync, editing, and utility workflows.
Provides belt CLI examples for Veo, Seedance, HappyHorse, Wan, Grok, OmniHuman, Fabric, PixVerse, Topaz, and HunyuanVideo.
Shows required input fields for prompts, image URLs, audio URLs, video URLs, duration, resolution, and audio generation.
Guides users to browse video apps with the belt app store category filter.
Connects related skills for avatars, text-to-speech, image generation, and social posting workflows.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and a valid authenticated account.
Does not generate videos locally; external services process prompts and media references.
Costs, rate limits, model availability, duration, and resolution depend on inference.sh apps.
Example media URLs are placeholders and must be replaced with accessible user assets.

use_cases.title: Create Campaign Clips
use_cases.description: Create short campaign clips from text prompts, product photos, or reference images using suitable video models.

use_cases.title: Build Media Pipelines
use_cases.description: Plan repeatable video workflows that combine generated footage, foley sound, upscaling, and merged clips.

use_cases.title: Produce Avatar Demos
use_cases.description: Animate portraits or product images with voice audio for demos, tutorials, or social posts.

prompt_templates.title: Generate First Clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short text-to-video plan for a 5-second product teaser. Recommend one fast model and the needed belt inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Animate One Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me animate a product image with gentle camera motion. Choose an image-to-video model and list the media URL requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Create Talking Avatar
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an avatar video from a portrait and narration audio. Recommend a model and explain what assets I need before running belt.

prompt_templates.title: Build Video Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an advanced workflow for three clips, foley sound, upscaling, and a final merge. Include model choices and execution order.

output_examples.input: I need a 5-second social video from a product prompt.
output: Recommended approach: Use a fast text-to-video model first, then rerun on a higher quality model if the concept works.
Expected result: A concise belt workflow with model choice, prompt guidance, duration, and audio options.

output_examples.input: I have a portrait and narration audio for a demo.
output: Recommended approach: Use an avatar or lipsync model that accepts image and audio URLs.
Expected result: A checklist of assets, model fit, and privacy warnings before generation.

output_examples.input: I need to improve a silent generated clip.
output: Recommended approach: Add foley sound, upscale the video, then merge clips only after reviewing each result.
Expected result: A staged workflow that keeps quality checks between each external processing step.

best_practices: Use non-sensitive prompts and media unless your organization approves the provider and data handling.
Start with fast or economical models before using higher quality settings.
Check each model's current cost, duration, resolution, and input requirements before running belt.
anti_patterns: Do not send confidential images, voices, or unpublished videos without approval.
Do not assume every listed model supports the same inputs or audio options.
Do not use placeholder URLs or private files that the external service cannot access.

faq.question: Does this skill create video inside Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: No. It helps those tools plan and run inference.sh video workflows through the belt CLI.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples require the belt CLI and authentication before running video apps.

faq.question: Can it animate images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill lists image-to-video models and shows which inputs use image URLs.

faq.question: Can it make talking avatar videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It references OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse workflows that use portrait and audio inputs.

faq.question: Can it edit or upscale existing video?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes video editing, foley, upscaling, and media merging app examples.

faq.question: What should I avoid uploading?
faq.answer: Avoid sensitive images, voices, private videos, and confidential prompts unless provider use is approved.
